Build one multi-row INSERT and its bound parameters

dot-build_insert_chunk.Rd

Split out of [.db_append_table()] so the placeholder layout can be tested without a database connection. Takes identifiers already quoted, and so does no quoting of its own.

Usage

.build_insert_chunk(quoted_table, quoted_cols, chunk)

Arguments

quoted_table

Character(1). Already-quoted table identifier.

quoted_cols

Character(1). Already-quoted, comma-separated column list, in the same order as the columns of `chunk`.

chunk

A data frame of at least one row.

Value

A list with `sql` and `params`.

Details

Placeholders are laid out **column-major**: row `i` of column `j` is `$((j-1)*k + i)` for a chunk of `k` rows. That is what allows `params` to be the columns concatenated — one `as.list()` per column — rather than a loop over every cell, which matters when a chunk holds tens of thousands of values.
